question: Where in frozen video-transformer encoders do intuitive-plausibility and elementary motion variables become linearly accessible, and are those variables stored as compact factorized quantities or as distributed task-specific population codes?

key_findings.claim: The authors report a sharp intermediate-depth transition, called the Physics Emergence Zone, at which linear and attentive IntPhys accuracy rises from near chance to roughly 85–95 percent across several sufficiently large encoders.
key_findings.evidence: Layerwise probes on V-JEPA 2 Large, Huge, and Giant and VideoMAEv2 Giant show a similar breakpoint near one third of network depth; smaller VideoMAE variants do not reproduce it. Matched possible and impossible clips diverge around the violation breakpoint at the same layers.

key_findings.claim: Scalar speed and acceleration magnitude are linearly readable early, whereas motion direction becomes readable only around the reported emergence zone.
key_findings.evidence: Probes on controlled Kubric ball videos decode Cartesian and polar motion variables across depth. Speed and acceleration-magnitude curves rise early, while direction changes sharply at intermediate depth; a multi-object CLEVRER probe shows a similar direction profile.

anchors.section: Appendix / patch and object-level direction decoding

key_findings.claim: The measured linear subspaces for direction and intuitive plausibility are nearly orthogonal, but this does not establish that the underlying computation is independent or non-factorized.
key_findings.evidence: Principal angles are reported around 69–83 degrees; projecting direction into the IntPhys probe span preserves only 7–13 percent and speed less than 3 percent, near random-subspace controls. These tests cover fitted linear readouts, so a nonlinear or upstream shared state remains possible.

key_findings.claim: Suppressing local spatial or temporal attention at the emergence layer reduces motion-direction and IntPhys readout, but the ablation is too broad to localize a physics-specific circuit.
key_findings.evidence: At the selected layer, direction R-squared falls from 0.97 to 0.93 under spatial suppression, 0.83 under temporal suppression, and 0.14 under their strongest combination; IntPhys falls from 78.3 to 62.2, 51.9, and 61.7 percent respectively, while ImageNet stays near 33 percent. No matched random-head, mask-volume, or off-layer ablation is reported.

key_findings.claim: Direction is organized as a circular population code spread over many MLP features rather than one axis in the tested linear basis.
key_findings.evidence: Individual units show sinusoidal directional tuning with phase offsets, and the population follows a circular geometry. Iterative orthogonal probing retains direction after many directions are removed, which the authors interpret as roughly 40–50 relevant features in representative layers.

key_findings.claim: The reported feature-count summary is internally inconsistent with the appendix table, weakening any exact dimensionality claim.
key_findings.evidence: The prose summarizes direction dimensions of roughly 66–136 and IntPhys dimensions of 7–15 in one analysis, whereas Table 3 lists direction dimension 400 at layers 20–23 and IntPhys values up to 32. Iterative probe counts also depend on an explicit accuracy threshold rather than estimating intrinsic dimension.

key_findings.claim: Multi-feature activation steering changes a held-out direction decoder much more than single-feature steering, but it is not evidence that video prediction or generation was physically controlled.
key_findings.evidence: The main text reports target-angle error below 0.5 degrees for coordinated steering versus above 80 degrees for one feature. The held-out appendix protocol shows 20-probe steering reducing mean angular error from 82.9 to 11.9 degrees on 103 test examples; the intervention is judged by another decoder and no downstream video, rollout, or planning behavior is measured.

key_findings.claim: The emergence signature is selective among the paper's controls, but the controls do not distinguish physical abstraction from generic temporal displacement processing.
key_findings.evidence: Counting, ImageNet, and Something-Something V2 probes do not show the same breakpoint, whereas detecting temporally shuffled video does. The study has no pixel, optical-flow, untrained-network, or random-weight control, even though direction and shuffling are directly recoverable from visual displacement cues.

key_findings.claim: A small predictor trained from each frozen layer performs best from intermediate features on one violation-of-expectation task, but can relearn the task from earlier representations.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix trains a new V-JEPA-style predictor from scratch on each encoder layer for a Garrido et al. task and shows its best qualitative curve in the middle layers. Early-layer performance remains substantial, and the paper gives no numerical table, uncertainty, or fixed-compute learning curves for the downstream predictors.

key_findings.claim: The experiments establish linear accessibility and coarse causal sensitivity in encoders, not that a video world model makes physically accurate predictions.
key_findings.evidence: Most experiments use frozen V-JEPA or VideoMAE encoders, synthetic ball trajectories, and IntPhys classification. The conclusion itself limits the claims to representation accessibility and partial causal influence and notes that these tests do not recover a complete circuit or general physical engine.

method.core_idea: Freeze several pretrained video encoders, localize where intuitive-plausibility and controlled motion labels become readable, then characterize the geometry, spatial distribution, attention dependence, and steerability of those readouts.
method.mechanism: The study extracts every encoder layer, fits grouped-cross-validated linear, nonlinear, and attentive probes on IntPhys, CLEVRER, and fixed-renderer Kubric trajectories, compares probe-weight subspaces with principal angles and projections, suppresses attention by spatial and temporal distance at a selected emergence layer, fits generalized-linear tuning curves to MLP units, repeatedly removes orthogonal probe directions, and injects coordinated activation changes toward target motion directions. A separate learned predictor consumes representations from different frozen depths.
assumptions: Linear or lightweight-probe accessibility is a meaningful indicator of encoded physical information rather than a dataset or renderer cue.
The chosen layer grid and breakpoint definition resolve a genuine computational transition.
Fixed-camera ball displacement requires a physical abstraction beyond optical flow or position differencing.
IntPhys possible and impossible clips are matched well enough that a probe cannot exploit local rendering discontinuities.
Principal angles between fitted linear probes reflect functional independence of the computations that produced them.
Iterative orthogonal probe removal estimates representation dimensionality despite threshold, regularization, and correlated-feature dependence.
Distance-based suppression changes the intended attention routes without introducing a generic out-of-distribution corruption.
A decoder that is held out from the intervention is sufficiently independent to establish meaningful steering.
Differences among V-JEPA and VideoMAE variants can be interpreted despite changes in objective, data, architecture, resolution, and capacity.
Results from toy synthetic motion and coarse plausibility violations transfer to natural, compositional physical prediction.

techniques.role: Maps when intuitive-plausibility and motion labels become linearly or attentively readable.
Varies direction, speed, acceleration, and start position under fixed rendering to label elementary kinematics.
Separates related trajectory groups while selecting among twenty probe configurations.
Compares the fitted linear spans for physical variables and plausibility.
Measures how much one task's decodable signal survives projection into another task's probe span.
Tests sensitivity to local spatial and temporal attention at a selected layer.
Fits circular direction tuning across individual MLP features.
Counts how many independently fitted linear directions can be removed before readout falls below a threshold.
Perturbs multiple direction-sensitive features jointly and evaluates a separately trained decoder.
Tests how useful each frozen layer is to a newly trained plausibility predictor.

evaluations.setting: IntPhys possible-versus-impossible videos across V-JEPA 2 Large, Huge, and Giant and VideoMAE/VideoMAEv2 variants
evaluations.metric: Layerwise linear and attentive probe accuracy
evaluations.result: Large successful encoders rise from near 50 percent to approximately 85–95 percent around one third depth; smaller VideoMAE variants do not consistently do so
evaluations.baseline: Chance, other encoder sizes, and non-physics probe tasks

evaluations.setting: Fixed-renderer Kubric ball trajectories and CLEVRER multi-object clips
evaluations.metric: Cross-validated R-squared or classification accuracy for velocity, acceleration, speed, magnitude, and direction
evaluations.result: Scalar magnitudes are accessible early while direction rises at intermediate depth and shows a similar profile across single- and multi-object settings
evaluations.baseline: Earlier and later encoder layers; no pixel or optical-flow baseline

evaluations.setting: Direction, speed, and IntPhys fitted probe subspaces
evaluations.metric: Principal angles and retained signal after projection
evaluations.result: Direction-versus-IntPhys angles are about 69–83 degrees; direction retains 7–13 percent and speed less than 3 percent in the plausibility span

evaluations.setting: Attention suppression at the selected emergence layer
evaluations.metric: Direction R-squared, IntPhys accuracy, and ImageNet accuracy
evaluations.result: Baseline 0.97/78.3/33.7 changes to 0.93/62.2/33.5 for one spatial mask, 0.83/51.9/30.3 for one temporal mask, and 0.14/61.7/33.1 for their strongest combination
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified inference; no random-head or off-layer matched ablation

evaluations.setting: Held-out coordinated direction steering on 103 test examples
evaluations.metric: Mean target-angle error of a separately trained decoder
evaluations.result: Twenty-probe steering changes mean error from 82.9 to 11.9 degrees; the main-text best configuration is below 0.5 degrees
evaluations.baseline: No steering and single-feature intervention above 80 degrees

evaluations.setting: A newly initialized V-JEPA predictor trained from individual frozen encoder depths
evaluations.result: Intermediate inputs are qualitatively best, while early layers remain useful; exact values and uncertainty are not tabulated
evaluations.baseline: Predictors trained from other encoder depths

limitations: Author-stated: the study covers encoder representations and does not identify a complete mechanistic circuit or demonstrate an explicit symbolic physics engine.
Author-stated: most labeled motion experiments use a toy rendered ball, coarse variables, and fixed visual conditions; natural-scene physical reasoning may differ.
Author-stated: representation accessibility and the attention interventions establish only partial causal influence.
Reviewer-identified: neither next-frame physical accuracy nor closed-loop prediction, planning, or generation is evaluated, so the term world model is broader than the evidence.
Reviewer-identified: direction in a fixed-camera rendered scene is visually available through displacement; no pixels, optical flow, untrained network, or random-weight encoder is tested.

Reviewer-identified: IntPhys probes may exploit violation-frame discontinuities or rendering artifacts because there is no cross-generator, cross-violation, appearance-matched, or breakpoint-held-out test.
Reviewer-identified: objective comparisons are confounded by architecture, data, preprocessing, capacity, and model size.
Reviewer-identified: linear subspace separation cannot exclude a shared nonlinear or upstream state, so it does not justify a general claim that the representation is non-factorized.
Reviewer-identified: iterative nullspace counts are threshold-dependent readout counts, not intrinsic dimensions, and the prose conflicts with Table 3.
Reviewer-identified: broad distance masks lack matched random-head, attention-volume, layer, and generic-corruption controls.
Reviewer-identified: steering is evaluated only by another learned decoder and not by a changed future trajectory or physical behavior.
Reviewer-identified: the downstream predictor can learn a new decoder from each layer, so its performance does not localize the frozen encoder's original computation.
failure_modes: A layer appears to contain physics because it makes local displacement or a rendering discontinuity easy to linearly classify.
A sharp probe transition reflects a generic representational scale change or normalization effect rather than a physics computation.
Two linear probes look orthogonal even though both depend on the same curved manifold or nonlinear latent state.
Iterative probe removal counts redundant linear separators and inflates the apparent feature dimension.
Attention suppression causes general temporal information loss or activation distribution shift that the probe reports as lost physics.
A coordinated feature injection satisfies the held-out decoder while moving off the natural activation manifold and producing no valid behavior.
The emergence depth changes or disappears under new renderers, camera motion, natural video, longer horizons, or different physical laws.
A small downstream predictor relearns plausibility from generic visual features, falsely validating the proposed layer localization.
Model-family differences are attributed to objectives even though data scale, tokenization, architecture, and resolution explain them.
High IntPhys accuracy fails to transfer to counterfactual prediction, continuous parameter extrapolation, contact dynamics, or embodied control.
reusable_insights: Map physical variables across every layer before interpreting only the final embedding; intermediate layers can carry stronger task structure.
Decompose kinematics into magnitudes and directions because their readout depths and representational geometry may differ.
Pair decodability with matched causal interventions, but evaluate interventions through independent behavior rather than the same probe family.
Use cross-task subspace controls as one diagnostic while explicitly retaining the possibility of shared nonlinear computation.
Test the same physical variable at patch, object, and scene scales to distinguish local motion cues from object-level state.
Treat coordinated population steering as a hypothesis about distributed coding and require on-manifold, rollout-level validation.
For physical world-model evaluation, add pixels, optical flow, random encoders, renderer shifts, and held-out physical regimes before naming a representation physical.
Report dimensionality as sensitivity across probe thresholds, regularizers, and seeds rather than a single count.
Contrast intermediate feature accessibility with end-to-end physical prediction so representation and behavior are not conflated.
open_questions: Does the reported emergence zone survive cross-renderer, moving-camera, real-video, and novel-law evaluation?
Can an untrained encoder, optical-flow pipeline, or pixels-only baseline reproduce the direction and IntPhys transitions?
Do the same layers causally determine physically correct future frames, plans, or generated trajectories?
Are direction and plausibility independent after nonlinear subspace, circuit, and activation-patching analyses?
How stable are the probe dimensions and population tuning across seeds, thresholds, regularization, and model revisions?
Which particular attention heads and MLP features matter under matched random, off-layer, and activation-norm controls?
Can steering remain on the natural activation manifold and change a decoded physical variable without degrading unrelated content?
Does a fixed small downstream learner preserve the intermediate-layer advantage under controlled compute and multiple seeds?
Can an emergence signature predict out-of-distribution physical extrapolation better than ordinary in-distribution probe accuracy?

competitive_landscape.title: Intuitive physics understanding emerges from self-supervised pretraining on natural videos
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest prior behavioral and representation-level antecedent for physics emerging in predictive video encoders.
competitive_landscape.difference: Garrido et al. compare objectives and training data through violation-of-expectation behavior, whereas this paper localizes and perturbs motion and plausibility readouts across layers; the antecedent already establishes the core emergence claim.

competitive_landscape.title: The Invisible Hand of Physics: When Video Diffusion Models Know More Than They Show
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct contemporary competitor probing physical plausibility across depth in generative video transformers.
competitive_landscape.difference: It approximately inverts diffusion trajectories and probes multiple denoising times, finding intermediate-depth readout and block sensitivity; this paper instead studies encoder layers, elementary feature geometry, attention masks, and feature steering.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Video Foundation Models Understand Intuitive Physics? A Layerwise Probing Analysis
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct contemporary layerwise-probing competitor spanning predictive, reconstruction, and diffusion video models.
competitive_landscape.difference: It compares four relative depths and stronger temporal probes on IntPhys 2 and MVP, while this paper supplies finer layer localization and representational interventions but on narrower synthetic physics labels.

competitive_landscape.title: Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct competing intervention framework that includes physical dynamics in a video world model.
competitive_landscape.difference: It tests whether on-manifold activation paths cause corresponding behavioral trajectories and reports linear steering can be unnatural; this paper's coordinated steering is evaluated only by a decoder and does not test behavior-manifold agreement.

competitive_landscape.title: Do generative video models understand physical principles?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct negative evidence about physical-law competence in video generators.
competitive_landscape.difference: Physics-IQ evaluates generated outcomes across fluid, optical, solid, magnetic, and thermal phenomena and finds realism does not imply physics; this paper studies internal encoder accessibility and therefore cannot resolve that behavior gap.

competitive_landscape.title: How Far is Video Generation from World Model: A Physical Law Perspective
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct controlled negative result on learning and extrapolating mechanics from video.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kang et al. measure in-distribution, combinatorial, and out-of-distribution generated trajectories and find case-based imitation rather than law abstraction; this paper decodes in-distribution kinematic variables without testing extrapolation.

competitive_landscape.title: IntPhys: A Framework and Benchmark for Visual Intuitive Physics Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational benchmark and possible-versus-impossible evaluation antecedent used by the paper.
competitive_landscape.difference: IntPhys defines matched violation-of-expectation scenes and future-mask baselines; this paper reuses its labels for internal localization, inheriting the benchmark's scope without adding cross-generator validity tests.

competitive_landscape.title: Physion: Evaluating Physical Prediction from Vision in Humans and Machines
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing human-grounded physical-prediction benchmark and contrary evidence about representation structure.
competitive_landscape.difference: Physion tests future contact across varied materials and finds object-centric models stronger while still below humans; this paper argues for distributed coding from linear subspaces but does not compare object-centric prediction or human behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: LikePhys: Evaluating Intuitive Physics Understanding in Video Diffusion Models via Likelihood Preference
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing model-internal evaluation that avoids relying only on generated visual quality.
competitive_landscape.difference: LikePhys ranks valid-invalid video pairs with a diffusion likelihood surrogate and validates alignment to human preference across twelve scenarios; this paper probes encoder activations and offers finer localization but no human-aligned output metric.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first direct interpretability study of physical representations inside large video encoders, identifying a cross-architecture Physics Emergence Zone and a high-dimensional, circular, causally steerable population code rather than factorized variables.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its combination of fine-grained layerwise motion decomposition, task-subspace comparison, patch localization, attention suppression, population tuning, iterative probe removal, and coordinated steering is broader than the prior violation-of-expectation studies.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: After Garrido et al., the emergence of intuitive-physics readout in predictive encoders is not new. The credible novelty is the within-encoder localization and descriptive geometry of direction plus preliminary interventions. Claims of a general non-factorized physical computation, a physics-specific causal circuit, and behaviorally effective control are not established by linear subspaces, broad attention masks, and decoder-only steering.

reviewer_notes: Full 33-page extraction read end to end. Author-reported results are separated above from reviewer inference and internal consistency checks. Primary arXiv records for nine direct or adverse competitors were checked on 2026-08-23. The paper is strong as a hypothesis-generating representation atlas, but its main nouns should be read narrowly: encoder, probe-accessible motion and plausibility, and selected interventions—not a validated physical simulator or compact mechanistic circuit.
